To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glutamate receptor trafficking is regulated by a novel mechanism in which the receptor is retained in the endoplasmical reticulum until a specific signal is received that triggers the receptor's exit to the cell surface.

1) Glutamate receptor trafficking to neuronal cell surfaces involves a regulated step in receptor exit from the ER, 2) This ER exit step is regulated by the ER chaperone calnexin, and 3) Calnexin is a critical component of the molecular machinery that controls the number and distribution of postsynaptic ionotropic glutamate receptors in the mammalian brain.
the exit of glutamate receptors from the endoplascmic reticulum represents an essential regulatory step in glutamte receptor trafficking to the cell surface.
